tasks.behavior: Docs and code text keep their place on Linux and Android while the fonts load
acceptance: On Chromium for Linux, /docs at 1440 px with every font file arriving late shifts less than 0.01
notes: 2026-10-30 review fail by reviewer: Root cause confirmed in the Linux browser (pw-linux-fonts): main's fonts.ts and globals.css fail docs.spec.ts:85 at 0.0889, HEAD passes. Main's build has next/font's face 'Hanken Grotesk Fallback; src local(Arial); 99.07% / 30.02% / 0.0% / 100.94%', so the copied overrides are exact. HEAD resolves --fw-font-sans-loaded to '"Hanken Grotesk", Hanken Grotesk Fallback' and --fw-font-sans still ends in system-ui, sans-serif. Lighthouse: 98 / 100 / LCP 1862 ms. check-docs: 0 errors. Docs lines are within 25 words. The test rename names what it holds. The kit select test fails the same way on main's code in that browser (scrollbar 0), so it comes from connect mode. Defect: display optional with subsets ['latin'] preloads only the latin Hanken face. In Chromium, an optional face that starts loading after the first paint is never used in that document. Linux probe on HEAD: text added after load ('Łukasz Wiśniewski'), latin-ext face fetched in 9 ms, still 'Liberation Sans:2, Hanken Grotesk:15' for the document's life (client navigations included). Hanken only shows after a reload. On main (swap) the same probe renders all Hanken. So client-rendered names with Polish, Czech, Turkish, Romanian or Hungarian letters mix two fonts inside one word, even on a fast connection. fonts.ts, DESIGN.md and the commit say a face shows when it arrives in the short wait, which is not true for these faces. Fix tried: subsets ['latin', 'latin-ext'] makes the probe all Hanken, keeps the shift test at 3 of 3 on Linux, and Lighthouse reads 98 / 100 / LCP 1946 ms. Then say in the docs which subsets are preloaded. Note: Noto Sans (document previews) still uses next's Arial-only fallback with swap. That is the same Linux fallback bug, limited to previews. Fix it or name it.

2026-10-30 review pass by reviewer: Latin-ext fix confirmed. HTML on / and /docs preloads 3 fonts: Hanken latin, Hanken latin-ext (19.5 KB), Geist Mono. Probe: 'Łukasz Wiśniewski' inserted after load draws 17 glyphs in Hanken on Linux (pw-linux-fonts) and macOS. With 800 ms font delay on Linux it draws in Liberation Sans, not DejaVu. Fallback faces read 'loaded' on Linux at HEAD; main on 3700 reads 'error' for both. Noto overrides 100.54/27.56/0/106.33 and Hanken's 99.07/30.02/0/100.94 match main's next/font CSS. docs.spec.ts passed in the Linux browser (6/6), font test 3/3 with --repeat-each 3. tasks.behavior: A closed or canceled pay link shows that it takes no money, without the network and token pickers

2026-10-30 review fail by reviewer: Bug reproduced on main (canceled payer-chooses invoice: Network combobox count 1) and fixed; pay+link-pay e2e 44 passed; docs-check 0 errors; 1440/390 screenshots look right. Defect 1 (a11y, money safety): in-session change from waiting (address shown) to canceled or expired loses the live region. A MutationObserver probe shows the persistent

'Waiting for payment' is removed and the root div gains role=status together with its new content; on main the same

stays and its text changes. A polite region that appears with its content is not reliably announced, so 'Do not send money.' can go unheard. The file's own rule: 'Always rendered, so the live region exists before a check finds money.' Keep one live region mounted across the change. Defect 2: per-option close (?option= or a kept pick on a closed option while another option is open, as in 'a closed payment option leaves another option available') now shows the Network/Token pickers and the full 'Checkout closed' empty state together, against the new DESIGN rule (one closed state, no pickers). The closed branch keys on pay.state, the pickers on canChoose; gate it on !canChoose or say that option closed. Minor: DESIGN and commit say 'Canceled ... with nothing seen', but a canceled invoice with held money also shows this state. toHaveText->toContainText is fine; the new test is an allowed user-hit regression test.

2026-10-30 review fail by reviewer: Code fixes confirmed; e2e pay+link-pay 45 passed; docs-check 0 errors. Fix 1 OK: StatusLine keeps its fiber slot and the role=status div is the same DOM node; a probe with key={shut ?? "row"} (forced remount) fails "a payer watching hears the payment close". p->div breaks no test or grid. Fix 2 code OK: closed state shows only when !canChoose; a mixed-option screenshot shows the pickers with the one-line row. Defect: the new guard in "a closed payment option leaves another option available" passes with the bug. getByText("Checkout closed") toHaveCount(0) runs right after goto, before the mocked invoice loads, so it passes at once. Probe: drop !choosable from shut; the test still passed. With await expect(Network combobox).toBeVisible() before it, it failed (Received: 1). With the real code it passed. Fix: move the assertion after the Network combobox is visible or clicked. The commit message says the test now expects no closed state; true, but it does not catch the defect.

2026-10-30 review pass by reviewer: Test-strength defect fixed: with '!choosable && ' removed from shut, 'a closed payment option leaves another option available' fails at pay.spec.ts:609 (Checkout closed count Expected 0, Received 1); restored (same sha1 de4f0a46), it passes. Diff re-read: canChoose excludes canceled; shut only when nothing can be picked; one persistent role=status region; PAY_STATES.closed is closed with nothing received, so 'expired with nothing seen' is right. Commit message matches the diff. Worktree clean.
